title: Pre-Roman Necropolis Reveals Secrets of Iron Age Mediterranean Diets
gist: Isotopes locked into bone and teeth preserve a chemical record of diet for tens of thousands of years; a new study applies that technique to Italy's 2,700-year-old Novilara necropolis, where men appear to have eaten more meat than women.

insights.claim: Isotopes from food are incorporated into bone and teeth and can persist for tens of thousands of years, letting archaeologists reconstruct what an individual ate from a unique chemical fingerprint.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Isotopic archaeology turns skeletal collections into quantitative datasets on ancient nutrition and inequality, expanding the addressable market for analytical mass-spectrometry services beyond clinical labs.
insights.quote: “you are what you eat” is literally true on a chemical level
insights.locator: Far from being just a glib reminder

insights.claim: The Novilara necropolis on Italy's northeastern coast, discovered in the late 19th century and holding hundreds of bodies, is 2,700 years old and predates Roman dominance of the region.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Large, long-excavated burial sites are being re-mined with new analytical methods, so legacy museum collections carry latent research value without new fieldwork cost.

insights.claim: Isotopic evidence from the Iron Age Novilara burials indicates that men in the community ate more meat than women did.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Gendered access to high-value protein in a pre-Roman community is evidence that dietary inequality tracks social hierarchy far back in history.
insights.quote: Spoiler alert: The men ate more meat

insights.claim: Grave goods at Novilara span elegant items such as ornate amber jewelry and weaponry alongside quotidian objects like spools and spindles, making the site a cross-section of an entire community rather than an elite-only burial ground.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A socially mixed sample lets researchers compare diets across status tiers within one population, which is where the interesting inequality signal lives.
insights.quote: Basically, Novilara is the final resting place for an interesting cross-section of people.
insights.locator: The bodies buried there were adorned
